important.name: Stale Pipfile re-enters main beside the uv environment
important.summary:
The merge base has pyproject.toml, uv.lock and .python-version and no Pipfile; the PR head adds Pipfile back (branch commits 8b00217/3de9eb1 never deleted it). Merging puts a second dependency manifest on main that already disagrees with the uv one: python_version = "3.13" against the 3.14 pin in .python-version, pytest listed as a runtime package as well as a dev package, and no python-docx, so a pipenv environment built from it cannot import conversion.changelog_docx. The PR's own summary states the opposite ("Pipfile | D | Deleted; its packages ... move to pyproject.toml"), so the file is a leftover duplicate of pyproject.toml.

Also (system_shape): At the PR head, Pipfile (new relative to the merge base) still defines a second environment manifest: python_version = "3.13" (Pipfile:16) against .python-version 3.14 and the ruff comment at pyproject.toml:29; no python-docx, so conversion/changelog_docx.py:29 (`import docx`) fails in a pipenv environment; and pytest listed as a runtime package (Pipfile:10) while pyproject.toml:14-17 keeps it in the dev group. The PR body states the opposite ("Replaces the Pipfile ... Pipfile | D | Deleted"), and branch history shows Pipfile was added (8b00217) and modified (3de9eb1) but never removed. Two divergent manifests mean the environment depends on which tool a developer reaches for.

Also (roast): Main deleted the Pipfile when PR #2 moved the project to uv (33fe6c3, 'migrate from pipenv to uv'). This branch replays the old pipenv commits (8b00217, 3de9eb1, copies of e23a68a/4a63892), so the head adds a 16-line Pipfile again. It contradicts the real manifest. It pins python_version 3.13, while .python-version and the pyproject ruff comment say 3.14. It lacks python-docx, which conversion/changelog_docx.py imports at module level. It lists pytest under both [packages] and [dev-packages]. Anyone who runs `pipenv install` from it gets an environment where `python -m conversion.changelog_docx` and tests/test_changelog_docx.py fail on import. The PR's own description lists Pipfile as 'D Deleted', so the merged tree does the opposite of what the PR claims. Two manifests for one project is one too many.
fix: Delete Pipfile from the branch (git rm Pipfile) so pyproject.toml and uv.lock stay the only dependency source, as the PR summary describes.
Delete Pipfile (`git rm Pipfile`): pyproject.toml plus uv.lock already carry every dependency it lists, so it is a stale duplicate manifest.

If pipenv support is intentionally kept, bring Pipfile in line with pyproject.toml: python_version = "3.14", add python-docx = ">=1.2.0", move pytest to [dev-packages] only, and correct the PR body's 'Deleted' row.
Delete Pipfile from the branch (git rm Pipfile) so pyproject.toml plus uv.lock stay the only dependency manifest, as main already has it.

minor.name: Inline links with a title or a parenthesized URL render as raw Markdown
minor.summary: The module docstring lists inline links as covered Markdown (changelog_docx.py:12-14). The inline-link alternative in _INLINE, \[(?P<ltext>[^\]]+)\]\((?P<lurl>[^)\s]+)\) at line 334, rejects a destination that contains whitespace or ')'. So [text](url "title") and URLs with parentheses fail that alternative and fall to the reference alternative. The reference does not resolve, so _bracketed writes a literal [text], and (url "title") follows as plain text with identifier detection applied. The Word document then shows the raw Markdown and no hyperlink.
fix: Extend the lurl group to accept an optional title, e.g. \((?P<lurl>[^)\s]+)(?:\s+(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'))?\), and drop the title.
Or narrow the docstring: inline links without a title and without ')' in the URL.

minor.name: Code spans inside link text lose their visible backticks
minor.summary:
add_spans says code spans get visible backticks (changelog_docx.py:531), and the module docstring promises code-like terms in Consolas wrapped in visible backticks (lines 3-5). A span can be both code and a link: _linked inline-parses link text, so [`fpm`](url) yields Span(code=True, url=url). add_spans sends every span with a url to _add_hyperlink, which adds span.text without the backticks. _format_run then gives the run Consolas and replaces the dark red with LINK_COLOR. The term renders as blue Consolas with no backticks, which contradicts both docstrings.

Also (overall): add_spans documents "code spans get visible backticks, links become hyperlinks", but a span that is both code and linked (Markdown [`config.json`](url): _linked keeps code=True from the inline code token) takes the url branch to _add_hyperlink, which writes span.text without backticks while _format_run still applies the Consolas code font. The rendered text then differs from every other code term in the document.
fix: In _add_hyperlink, build the run text the same way as the non-link path: paragraph.add_run(f"`{span.text}`" if span.code else span.text).
Or qualify the add_spans docstring and the module docstring: code spans inside link text render as link-colored Consolas without backticks.
In _add_hyperlink, write f"`{span.text}`" when span.code is set, matching the non-link branch of add_spans.
Or narrow the add_spans docstring to say code spans inside links keep the code font without backticks.
